# Beowulf — questions for the owner

Each entry: date · part · the question · what the run decided meanwhile.

- 2026-10-12 · beowulf-fitt-09 · Cruces rendered from the lexica and flagged as guesses in the notes: (a) 599–601 ac hē lust wigeð, swefeð ond sendeþ (`l` "bears lust, puts to sleep and sends", `i` "takes his pleasure, kills and sends (them off)"; sendeþ has no object and the apparatus offers Kemble's [on] lust wīgeð, Bugge's [on] lust þigeð and seven other readings of swefeð ond sendeþ; some editors cancel ic at 601); (b) 646–651 the time clauses (oþðe kept as "or", the apparatus has "oð þæt" and an inserted [ne] at 648; scaduhelma gesceapu rendered "shadow-helmed shapes", a guess at dusk); (c) 620–621 dǣl ǣghwylcne with duguþe ond geogoþe taken as "each share of the seasoned and the young", the construction loose; (d) 581 wiht fram þē … searonīða … brōgan (wiht as adverb or noun, fram þē "about you", brōgan number); (e) 586 [fela] (Klaeber, after the apparatus’s “Gr.1” and Sedgefield) against [geflites] (Kluge, Holthausen, Schücking, Chambers); (f) 574 mid sweorde ofslōh (Rieger mēce, Holthausen ābrēat); (g) 565 brontne ford rendered "steep strait" and ȳðlāfe "wave-leaving", both guesses; also lāðgetēonan (559), swaþredon (569), fāra feng (578), hēafodmǣgum (583, "nearest kin"), werhðo (588, "damnation"), ealdre þīnum (590, "chief", the other reading being "life"), the odd genitive lēode in ēower lēode (596) and lēode Deniga (599), nȳdbāde (598, "forced-toll"), sweglwered (606, "sky-clad"), cynna gemyndig (613), the half-line order at 643, and hǣl against healle at 653. Glossary: the shared entries for wiste, wit, wan, ful, þearf, hǣl, aldre, gēoce, duguþe, geogoþe, ealle, eall, hīo, næs and lēode do not fit this part and are broadened. Decided meanwhile: published as flagged.

- 2026-10-14 · beowulf-fitt-26 · Cruces rendered from the lexica and flagged as guesses/disputed in the notes: 1878–80 ac him on hreþre hygebendum fæst / æfter dēorum men dyrne langað / born wið blōde (Klaeber’s italic ‘o’ in born, MS beorn; read as the preterite of beornan with langað a noun, “a hidden longing … burned”; the MS reading would make beorn “warrior” the subject of a verb langað, and Grein, Wyatt and Chambers read bearn “child”; wið blōde rendered “against the blood”, with “in the body’s blood”, “against the claim of kinship” and a loose “in” all left open; æfter dēorum men taken as “for the dear man”); 1841 wigtig (taken as a spelling of wītig “wise”, cf. wītig Drihten 1554; the alternative from wīg “war” noted) and sende (past, mood not shown by the form, rendered plain “sent”); 1822–25 þīnre mōdlufan māran tilian, gūðgeweorca (māran taken as the noun “more” with a genitive, not as “greater” agreeing with mōdlufan; the genitive gūðgeweorca rendered “by deeds of war” without knowing what it hangs on); 1830–31 Ic on Higelāce wāt with Gēata dryhten, folces hyrde in apposition to a dative (Kluge/Sedgefield dryhtne; Trautmann/Holthausen Higelāc); 1836–37 geþingeð (lemma uncertain, “resorts”) and the referent of him (Higelac, not Hrethric reflexive); 1850 þæt þe (particle read, not the pronoun) and sēlran … cyning ǣnigne, hordweard hæleþa (general or aimed at Beowulf); 1854 leng swā wēl (Grein, Holthausen, Schücking, Sedgefield sēl; “E.” bet, taken as Earle; Bugge bet or sēl); 1857 gemǣne (Sievers; MS ge mænum); 1862 hringnaca (“ring-boat”, the picture guessed), heafu (MS hea þu), luftācen (found nowhere else in the poem); 1868 [h]ine (MS inne, Thorkelin hine; the reason for the italic e not given); 1873–75 ōþres swīðor (“more than the other”, a genitive with comparative and no ‘than’; could mean the other man expected more), h[ī]e (MS he) and [nō] (Bugge, Sievers, Holthausen, Sedgefield, Chambers nā); 1871 ðegn[a] betstan (Kemble’s genitive plural added); 1883 āge[n]dfreân (MS aged-frean; the circumflex is low-confidence at transcription, placed on the second vowel); 1884 geæhted (“esteemed/praised”, lexica only) and on gange (“on the way” or “in progress”); 1887 sē þe oft manegum scōd (masculine sē with feminine yldo; Grein and others sēo; read as old age, with the king not excluded). Also: the shared glossary entries for bēo (“imperative singular” only; here 1st singular present, 1825), gesōhte (3rd singular preterite only; here a plural participle, 1839), geworhte (preterite only; here a plural participle, 1864) and ealdor (nominative only; here accusative, 1848) do not cover this part’s uses. Decided meanwhile: published as flagged; the owner may revisit.
